_about: Sourced inputs and assumptions for the illustrative national funnel. Input verification describes the cited figures; the chained output is a scenario.

access.metric: U.S. high school students with computer science available at their school
access.source: CSTA, 2024 State of Computer Science Education
access.source_short: CSTA, 2024 State of Computer Science Education
access.notes: Reported share of students with access. This is a student share rather than the share of schools offering CS.

high-school.metric: U.S. public school enrollment in grades 9–12
high-school.notes: Rounded as published (about 15.6 million). Covers the 50 states and D.C.

cs-enrollment.metric: Reported U.S. public school computer science enrollees in grades 9–12 or equivalent
cs-enrollment.notes: Sum of the 14 national cells in the Stage 2 charts. Covers female and male counts in the 50 states and D.C.

ap-csp.metric: AP Computer Science Principles takers in grades 9–12
ap-csp.notes: Sum of the four grade counts in the Computer Science Principles row. The program-wide count includes private and international students.

college-entry.metric: Estimated immediate four-year college entry for students averaging 3 across AP exams
college-entry.source: College Board, New Analyses of AP Scores of 1 and 2
college-entry.source_short: College Board, New Analyses of AP Scores of 1 and 2
college-entry.notes: The college enrollment chart reports a modeled probability for students with an average AP score of 3 across AP subjects.

cs-major.metric: CS major declarations among matched AP CSP takers at four-year colleges
cs-major.source: College Board, AP CSP and the STEM and Computer Science Pipelines
cs-major.source_short: College Board, AP CSP and the STEM and Computer Science Pipelines
cs-major.notes: Figure 2. The sample was limited to four-year college entrants who declared a major.

bachelor-completion.metric: Six-year bachelor’s completion among first-time, full-time bachelor’s seekers
bachelor-completion.notes: Bachelor’s completion within six years at the starting institution, across fields of study.

cs-degree-holders.metric: People whose highest degree was a computer and information sciences bachelor’s
cs-degree-holders.source: NCSES National Survey of College Graduates, Table 1-1
cs-degree-holders.source_short: NCSES National Survey of College Graduates, Table 1-1
cs-degree-holders.notes: The bachelor’s row for computer and information sciences includes employed and unemployed people and those outside the labor force.

computing-workers.metric: Computing and mathematical scientists whose highest degree was a computer and information sciences bachelor’s
computing-workers.source: NCSES National Survey of College Graduates, Table 1-2
computing-workers.source_short: NCSES National Survey of College Graduates, Table 1-2
computing-workers.notes: The bachelor’s row for computer and information sciences, computer and mathematical scientists column.

steps.label: Can take CS at school
steps.notes: Uses the published share of U.S. high school students with access to a CS course.

steps.label: Enroll in a high school CS course
steps.notes: Divides reported CS enrollment by estimated enrollment at schools offering CS. This assumes reported enrollees are part of the population with access. The two collections define course coverage differently.

steps.label: Take the AP CS Principles exam
steps.notes: Uses the ratio of program-wide AP CSP takers in grades 9–12 to U.S. public-school CS enrollees. Different school coverage makes this a rough proxy. It can include students who took CS in an earlier year.

steps.label: Enter a four-year college
steps.notes: Uses the four-year college entry estimate for 2017 graduates who averaged 3 across AP exams in any subject as a proxy for AP CSP takers. Two-year entry is outside this path.

steps.label: Earn a CS bachelor’s degree
steps.notes: Multiplies the share declaring CS in a matched AP CSP study by the overall six-year bachelor’s completion rate. This assumes those declaring CS keep that major and complete at the overall rate.

steps.label: Work in computing or math
steps.notes: Uses the share of people whose highest degree was a CS bachelor’s who worked as computer and mathematical scientists. The survey covers all career stages.
